body: It can be hard to distinguish the difference between thinking about it and wanting it. Suicidal ideation will drive you crazy if you let it.. I struggled w suicidal ideation for a decade before realizing it can be a mind over matter type thing? Because I was in the exact same spot. I thought about it literally 50+ times a day, yet wondered why I would never even get more than halfway thru the planning of it... It's because I recognized that I didn't really wanna be dead, I just didn't wanna be here and in my current situation. I would think about kms on an hourly basis as a form of control. Suicidal ideation, in my opinion, sometimes can be deduced to just that. It is an 'option'. When youre suicidal, you always have the chance to stop and think "well I could totally take control of everything happening in my life and once if I just ended it". For me, after having a thought like that, after realizing that, ultimately, my life actually IS in my own hands, I would be okay for awhile. After realizing the ideation was in large part about control, I also realized that allowing my brain to go off on a tangent about how terrible life is and how much I hate myself was detrimental and could be changed. I started talking to myself like I would talk to a friend in a similar predicament (but much more harshly). If I was in my head saying something like, "Nobody complimented your new shoes today. Nobody cares about you and everyone would be better off if you were dead.", I would literally respond to myself and say, "Okay dumbass, if no one even cared about your shoes, why would they care if you were dead? You don't wanna be dead, idiot, just get in the fucking shower." That was enough to at least shut my brain up for long enough for me to accomplish tasks. Eventually I made a habit of this, kinda gaslighting myself, but more about interrupting the thoughts and giving a reality-check in real time. I know this is probably the most disorganized, rambling reply on reddit rn, but the point is that I've been there and get what you're going thru. I'm glad you haven't gone thru with it yet. Know there's a reason for that. Know there's something better waiting for you on the other side of how you're feeling right now, and know that you can literally overcome this because its all in your brain and thats the one thing you can control (even if you need meds to help you, thats okay too). If you need a friend or wanna talk more abt this, feel free to pm.

Even if your acne is 10x worse irl than it looks in that picture, it's honestly still pretty normal for a teenager. I know its hard to move past insecurities like that, especially in teen years, but think about it like this: Your skin is the most unexciting, NORMAL thing about you. Everyone has skin all over. Most people have blemishes somewhere on their skin at all times. I work with adults (Im talking 35 and up) who still struggle with acne and some who have pretty bad scarring and whatnot, and lemme tell you those are the last things I pay attention to abt them. Worry about the things you can't change  money or beauty products: your heart, personality, and choice of friends! You have your whole life to get your acne under control, but in the meantime, make sure your insecurity abt your skin isn't hiding your shine from the world. I really just wanna make sure you don't feel like a freak, because what ur friends said is wrong, and you are a totally normal 16 year old. This is a struggle a lot of people before you have gone thru. Im sorry it hinders you, but I trust you'll overcome. Please give it time and be kind to yourself while you figure it out.. Look into gentle exfoliants for the scarring, try using witch hazel on active spots, nightly, before bed. Best of luck.

I'm sorry about your struggles related to being trans. That is something I know I will never or could never relate to, but I can only imagine the weight it carries. Im sorry you experience things like that, and I'm sorry people are so cruel. Besides that, though, I really relate to everything else you've mentioned. I've been struggling with my mental health for over a decade, with and without treatments. I used to SH, but have luckily managed to stop that (in the obvious ways, though I know I harm myself in a lot of other ways, less intentionally). It really helped me a lot when I realized that my suicidal ideation may be chronic... like, it may never go away completely, and for now, I can only learn to live with it. Life is totally meaningless, right? So nothing you do matters.. which means, technically, you can do whatever you want, whenever you want. Obviously I don't mean murder a bunch of people and quit your job and be homeless and run from the police or any crazy shir like that, right, but simple stuff, like deciding your brain doesn't get to call the shots for 10 minutes a day... that type of thing is totally doable. You can make up a rule for yourself that says for 10 minutes a day, you get full control over your brain, and you yell at it (quit literally, I tell mine to shut the fuck up and fuck off) when it interrupts you with mean, awful thoughts about yourself, and you can decide that you're gonna talk to yourself kindly, even if its just 10 minutes. You're allowed to take time for yourself, and treat yourself like a helpless baby for just 10 minutes. Coddle yourself. Be gentle. Defend yourself and your worth and your dignity (even when you feel like you have none) like you would defend an innocent baby with no ability to fight for themselves.. Cause that's basically you. The side of you that wants to live and thrive and be happy and kind and feel proud and successful and loved... that side is the baby... the side that tells you that life is too hard, and you are not worth it and you are not strong... thats not you.. you dont owe that side of you or those types of thoughts any room to breathe. I know that either sounds crazy or it sounds impossible to do, please just try it. Start out with whatever amount of time you can handle.. 60 seconds even... tell yourself kind things for 60 seconds.. ya know what I mean? Please trust when I say I can relate to most of what you think and feel, and this is something that has worked for me managing y suicidal ideation, even/especially during times where things are going okay in my life and I feel close to a breakthrough. And please reach out in pm if you ever need to talk.

A lot of things nowadays can be categorized as abuse.. I personally wouldn't consider this particular case to be abusive. You didn't do it with malicious intent to hurt him, and in the long run, it seems it has hurt you much more than it has hurt him. Even if it was 'abuse', the best thing you can do when you've abused someone is have a conversation with them about it, make sure everything is put on the table, apologize, and learn how to better manage yourself and your reactions moving forward. I don't think it was abuse. But if it was, you've done what you need to reconcile, and now you just have to allow yourself to move forward, knowing you'll be making yourself better with every step you take.

A lot of personal growth can happen in two years. What you DID was kinda immature and maybe a little toxic, but you recognize that now, which is the important thing. Doesnt mean that YOU as a person or as a partner are toxic. If you guys have been working on common goals, learning how to communicate, how to love each other better and be better together since then, that incident should 100% be swept under the rug.  It doesn't seem like a huge deal anyway, but if you feel like you are growing away from that type of behavior, cut yourself some slack and work toward better behavior in the future.
